question: What was the Counter-Reformation, and which council was its theological centerpiece?

choices.A: The Catholic Church's internal reform and doctrinal response to Protestantism, centered on the Council of Trent (1545-1563)
choices.B: A military campaign led by the pope to reconquer Protestant territories by force
choices.C: A movement within Protestantism to return to Catholic sacramental practice
choices.D: The reforms of the Second Vatican Council in response to modern secularism

teaching.title: The Counter-Reformation and Council of Trent
teaching.body: The Counter-Reformation (Catholic Reformation) was the Church's multi-faceted response to Protestantism: (1) doctrinal — the Council of Trent (1545-1563) defined Catholic teaching on Scripture, Tradition, justification, the sacraments, and more; (2) institutional — abuses of indulgences, clerical education, and pastoral practice were reformed; (3) missionary — new religious orders like the Jesuits (Ignatius of Loyola, 1540) drove evangelization; (4) spiritual — Teresa of Avila, John of the Cross, and Philip Neri led mystical and parish renewal. Trent shaped Catholicism until the Second Vatican Council (1962-1965).
